question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English Trade Growth — Bengal Factories / Location]
options: Hooghly — Site of an early English factory in Bengal, established in 1651
Kasimbazar — An important English factory town located in Bengal, known for silk trade
Patna — English factory in Bihar (part of the Bengal Presidency zone), important for saltpetre trade
Masulipatnam — English Bengal factory established as the gateway to the Bay of Bengal delta
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam is NOT a Bengal factory. It is on the Coromandel coast (present-day Andhra Pradesh). Bengal factories were at Hooghly, Kasimbazar, Patna, Balasore, etc.
explanation: English factories in Bengal were established at Hooghly (1651), Kasimbazar, Patna, and Balasore, among others. These formed the Bengal cluster of English trade. Masulipatnam (also spelled Machilipatnam) is on the Coromandel coast in the Krishna delta region of present-day Andhra Pradesh — it was the first English factory on the eastern coast (established 1611), predating Madras, but it is unambiguously a Coromandel factory, not a Bengal one.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English Trade Growth — Key Commodities & Routes]
options: Bengal — Exported raw silk, fine muslins (Dacca muslin), and saltpetre to Europe
Surat — Major entrepôt for cotton textiles and indigo from the Mughal hinterland
Malabar (Kerala) coast — Chief source of pepper and other spices for the English trade
Masulipatnam — Centre for Bengal's indigo trade due to its location on the Ganges delta
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam is NOT on the Ganges delta and is NOT a centre for Bengal's indigo trade. It is on the Coromandel coast in the Krishna-Godavari delta region of Andhra Pradesh. Bengal's indigo was traded through factories like Hooghly and Kasimbazar.
explanation: The Ganges delta (Sundarbans region) is in Bengal/Bangladesh. Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) lies in the Krishna-Godavari delta on the Coromandel coast. Bengal was indeed famous for raw silk, fine muslin (Dacca muslin), and saltpetre. Surat was an entrepôt for cotton textiles and indigo from the Mughal interior. The Malabar coast (Kerala) was the primary pepper-producing zone. These are all correctly matched except the false claim about Masulipatnam and Bengal indigo.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English Trade Growth — Regulatory Milestones]
options: Charter of 1600 — Granted the English East India Company exclusive trading rights east of the Cape of Good Hope
Regulating Act of 1773 — Made Calcutta the seat of the Governor-General of India
Pitt's India Act of 1784 — Established dual control of the Company by the Board of Control (Crown) and Court of Directors
Charter Act of 1813 — Ended the Company's exclusive trading monopoly over all Indian trade including the China tea trade
wrong_fact: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over Indian trade (except China). The China trade monopoly (including tea) was abolished only by the Charter Act of 1833, not 1813.
explanation: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over trade with India (except for the China trade and the tea trade, which continued until 1833). The Charter Act of 1833 finally threw open trade with China and abolished the tea monopoly. The original Charter of 1600 granted the EIC exclusive rights east of the Cape of Good Hope. The Regulating Act of 1773 created the position of Governor-General based at Calcutta. Pitt's India Act of 1784 established the Board of Control for political oversight alongside the Court of Directors.
